title: Find and Compare with Percentages
objective: I can find the percent of a number using an equation or a model.
model: tape diagram / double number line for the percent of a whole, and the equation Part = Percent × Whole with the percent written as a decimal

widgets.component: static tape of equal blocks, each labeled with its value; type '20% of 60 ='
widgets.root: The tape caption prints 'N block(s) × unit = answer' (e.g. '3 block(s) × 14 = 42') and the 'Model Breakdown' box beside it states the same arithmetic, so the number to type is on screen. Every block is already labeled with its value, so the student never finds one block. The tab is titled 'Visual Tape Diagrams & Double Number Lines' but no double number line is drawn, and nothing can be manipulated.
widgets.replacement: Rebuild as an interactive tape: the student chooses how many equal parts the whole is cut into (2, 4, 5, 10) with a stepper, the tape redraws unlabeled, the student taps blocks to shade the asked percent, and the tape prints only the shaded count and the shaded percent; the value of one block and the answer are typed. Add the double number line under the tape (amount above, percent below, aligned at 0 and the whole). Delete the caption and the Model Breakdown line.

widgets.where: Practice Tab 2 (8: decimal, then decimal × whole)
widgets.component: Part = Percent × Whole in two typed steps (25% of 80, 35% of 60, 8% of 50, 4% of 75, 65% of 200, 85% of 80 …)
widgets.root: This is the formula the lesson derives, in its own worked-example order (percent -> decimal -> multiply); all eight parts verified (20, 21, 6, 4, 130, 3, 54, 68). The 8% and 4% rows catch the 0.8 / 0.04 slip.

widgets.where: Practice Tab 3 (8: compare two percents of different wholes, three-choice mc)
widgets.component: 60% of 50 games versus 70% of 40, band 40% of 600 versus 50% of 450, discount deals, quizzes, solar arrays
widgets.root: Each option card prints its computed part ('= 30', '= 28') beneath the sentence, so the student compares two printed numbers and never finds a percent of a number; the correct choice is also the only one containing the two numbers ('30 > 28').
widgets.replacement: Hide the '= value' lines. Add the two-input Tab 2 form to each option (decimal, product) and unlock the choice only after both parts are entered; make the three choices the same shape ('Team Thunder', 'Team Lightning', 'same') with no numbers, so the comparison comes from the student's own products. Keep the real misconceptions as distractors (bigger percent wins; bigger whole wins).

widgets.where: Practice Tab 4 items t4_1, t4_3-t4_8 (battery, hoodie, tip, tax, attendance, low-power mode)
widgets.root: Discount, tip, tax and attendance are the lesson's contexts and the answers are right (3 h, $9, $36, $9, $3, 228, 5 h).

widgets.where: Practice Tab 4 item t4_2 ('Reveal Battery: 2 Bars Remaining')
widgets.component: 'what percent is charged, and how many hours remain (out of 15)?' with one answer box
widgets.root: The prompt asks for two quantities (percent charged = 40%, hours remaining = 6) but the single input is graded against 6; a student who types the percent is marked wrong with 'Review the percent equation'.
widgets.replacement: Split into two fields (Percent charged ___ %, Hours remaining ___) and grade both, or drop the percent clause and ask only 'How many hours remain?'.

widgets.component: 30% of 90, 6% as 0.06, 75% of 48, Green versus Blue art students, 10% of 350, 25% off $80, sale price, 3 of 5 bars, 5% of 60, 'higher percent always means more'
widgets.root: On objective; keys correct; the last item is a worthwhile conceptual check.

widgets.where: Practice Bonus Round (gen partOf how=decimal, 4 rounds)
widgets.root: Ties the percent, its decimal multiplier and the part; every trio generated from the numbers, one trio uses 45% of 20 = 9.
Same two-step form with percents above 100 and below 1; values verified (112, 80, 6, 12, 144, 30, 93.5, 117).

widgets.where: Challenge Tab 2 (8 matrices, 3 rows each, rate × base)
widgets.root: The 'Calculated Output' column prints every product ('45% × 120 = 54'), so the whole task is picking the largest printed number; no row is computed by the student.
widgets.replacement: Blank the Output column and give each row a numeric input; unlock the question after all three rows are correct. Keep the tie item (Room Y and Room Z) and add a row where the largest rate has the smallest whole.

widgets.where: Challenge Tab 3 (8: 30% off after 20% off, double markdown, 50% + 50%, discount then 8% tax, deal comparison, BOGO 50%, rebate versus instant, +10% then −10%)
widgets.root: The mathematics is right ($72, $120, $20, $291.60, $35.00 versus $36.13, 25%, Store B, $99) and a useful stretch of Part = Percent × Whole, but the correct choice always carries its working in brackets and the distractors are bare ($68, $130), so it can be found by form.
widgets.replacement: Same-shape choices (a dollar amount each), the working moved to the feedback; add a typed 'first price after the first discount' field before the choice so the sequencing is the student's.

widgets.where: Challenge Tab 4 (6: 4.5% commission, 18.5% drain for 2 hours, tiered 3% + 2%, 4.2% interest, 85% usable, 3.5% + 1.5% bonus)
widgets.root: Part = Percent × Whole with decimal percents and a tiered rate; all keys verified (1,260; 1,480; 7,000; 210; 2,975; 6,000). Two labels are off: the interest story is titled 'Compound Yield' for a one-year simple-interest calculation, and the bonus story hands the student the combined rate (5%).

widgets.where: Challenge Tab 5 (10 mc quiz) and Bonus Round (gen partOf how=decimal, 4 rounds up to 250% of 18)
widgets.component: 125% of 80, 0.5% of 2,400, discount comparison, stacked 20%, 250% of 16, commission, 5 segments, 0.2% of 5,000, 50% of 90 versus 90% of 50, average drain

typography: Practice Tab 4 explanations print '$45 - $9 = $36' and '$80 - $20 = $60' with hyphen-minus
Challenge Tab 3 and Tab 5 explanations print '$200 - $50', '$110 - $11', '3,500 - 525', '$80 - $16', '80% - 20%' with hyphen-minus
